title: String Functions
summary: Measure, clean up, cut, and build text with PostgreSQL's string functions.
intro: Real text is messy: stray spaces, shouting capitals, emails and phone numbers packed into one value. PostgreSQL has a function for each cleanup job, and you nest them to clean, cut, and rebuild text right inside a SELECT.
setup:
CREATE TABLE people (id integer, first_name text, last_name text, email text, phone text);
INSERT INTO people (id, first_name, last_name, email, phone) VALUES
    (1, ' ada', 'Lovelace', 'Ada@Example.com', '555-0101'),
    (2, 'ALAN', 'Turing', 'Alan.Turing@Bletchley.org', '555-0102'),
    (3, 'grace ', 'hopper', 'grace.hopper@navy.mil', '555-0103'),
    (4, 'Linus', 'TORVALDS', 'linus@kernel.org', '555-0104'),
    (5, 'Margaret', ' Hamilton ', 'M.Hamilton@NASA.gov', '555-0105'),
    (6, 'tim', 'berners-lee', 'tim@w3.org', '555-0106');

steps.title: Case and length
steps.body:
Every query in this lesson reads one table of people. Some names were typed carelessly, with stray spaces and odd letter case:

```sql
CREATE TABLE people (id integer, first_name text, last_name text, email text, phone text);
-- (1, ' ada', 'Lovelace', 'Ada@Example.com', '555-0101')
-- (2, 'ALAN', 'Turing', 'Alan.Turing@Bletchley.org', '555-0102')
-- (3, 'grace ', 'hopper', 'grace.hopper@navy.mil', '555-0103')
-- ... 6 rows in all, phones run up to '555-0106'
```

String functions take text and return new text, so you can nest them. The table itself never changes.

- `length(s)` counts characters, spaces included.
- `upper(s)` and `lower(s)` change every letter.
- `initcap(s)` capitalizes the first letter of each word and lowercases the rest.
- `trim(s)` removes spaces from both ends, never from the middle. `ltrim` and `rtrim` do one end.

```sql
SELECT initcap(trim('  grace HOPPER ')), length('  hi  ');
-- Grace Hopper | 6
```

Clean first, then measure: `length(trim(name))` counts only the real letters. Two gotchas: `initcap` turns `McDonald` into `Mcdonald`, and any of these functions given NULL returns NULL.

example.title: Tidy name list
example.prompt: Print each person's first name tidied up, the last name in capitals, and the first name's length before and after trimming.
example.code:
SELECT initcap(trim(first_name)) AS first,
    upper(trim(last_name)) AS last,
    length(first_name) AS raw_length,
    length(trim(first_name)) AS letters
FROM people
ORDER BY id;
example.output:
first   |    last     | raw_length | letters
----------+-------------+------------+---------
 Ada      | LOVELACE    |          4 |       3
 Alan     | TURING      |          4 |       4
 Grace    | HOPPER      |          6 |       5
 Linus    | TORVALDS    |          5 |       5
 Margaret | HAMILTON    |          8 |       8
 Tim      | BERNERS-LEE |          3 |       3
(6 rows)
example.explanation: `trim` runs first and removes the stray spaces, then `initcap` fixes the case. Compare `raw_length` with `letters`: ` ada` has 4 characters but only 3 letters, and `grace ` has a trailing space. Wrapping `last_name` in `trim` before `upper` matters for ` Hamilton `.

practice.prompt:

2. Select the number of characters in the email as `email_length`.

```text
(6 rows)
```

steps.title: Cutting text apart
steps.body:
To pull out a piece of text, pick the function that matches how you find the piece. Positions count from 1, not 0.

- `left(s, n)` and `right(s, n)` take the first or last `n` characters.
- `substring(s FROM start FOR count)` takes `count` characters starting at position `start`.
- `position(part IN s)` gives where `part` first appears, or 0 when it is missing.
- `split_part(s, delimiter, n)` splits on the delimiter and returns field `n`.

```sql
SELECT left('555-0101', 3), right('555-0101', 4),
    substring('Lovelace' FROM 2 FOR 3),
    position('@' IN 'ada@example.com'),
    split_part('ada@example.com', '@', 2);
-- 555 | 0101 | ove | 4 | example.com
```

`left(s, n)` is the same as `substring(s FROM 1 FOR n)`, but only `substring` can start in the middle. Use `split_part` when a separator marks the piece, like the `@` in an email. When the separator is missing, field 1 is the whole text and later fields are empty text. A negative field number counts from the end, so `split_part('a.b.c', '.', -1)` is `c`. A negative count in `left` or `right` drops characters instead: `left('hello', -2)` is `hel`. Trim first if the text may start with spaces, or `left` hands you a space.

example.title: Contact pieces
example.prompt: Print each person's initials, their email domain in lowercase, the first three digits of the phone, its last four digits, and where a dash appears in the last name.
example.code:
SELECT upper(left(trim(first_name), 1) || left(trim(last_name), 1)) AS initials,
    lower(split_part(email, '@', 2)) AS domain,
    substring(phone FROM 1 FOR 3) AS prefix,
    right(phone, 4) AS last_four,
    position('-' IN last_name) AS dash_at
FROM people
ORDER BY id;
example.output:
initials |    domain     | prefix | last_four | dash_at
----------+---------------+--------+-----------+---------
 AL       | example.com   | 555    | 0101      |       0
 AT       | bletchley.org | 555    | 0102      |       0
 GH       | navy.mil      | 555    | 0103      |       0
 LT       | kernel.org    | 555    | 0104      |       0
 MH       | nasa.gov      | 555    | 0105      |       0
 TB       | w3.org        | 555    | 0106      |       8
(6 rows)
example.explanation: `left(trim(...), 1)` takes the first real letter of each name, `||` joins the two, and `upper` capitalizes both. `split_part(email, '@', 2)` is everything after the `@`. The phone pieces sit at fixed positions, so `substring` and `right` cut them out directly. Only `berners-lee` has a dash, at position 8, so every other row gets 0.

practice.title: Email pieces
practice.prompt:
Print pieces of each person's email and last name from the people table.

1. Select the part of the email before the `@` as `username`.
2. Select the first 3 letters of the trimmed last name as `short_last`, using `substring`.
3. Select the position of the `@` in the email as `at_pos`.
4. Sort by `id`.

Expected output:

```text
   username   | short_last | at_pos
--------------+------------+--------
 Ada          | Lov        |      4
 Alan.Turing  | Tur        |     12
 grace.hopper | hop        |     13
 linus        | TOR        |      6
 M.Hamilton   | Ham        |     11
 tim          | ber        |      4
(6 rows)
```
practice.starter:
-- TODO: select username, short_last, and at_pos
SELECT email, last_name
FROM people
ORDER BY id;
practice.solution:
SELECT split_part(email, '@', 1) AS username,
    substring(trim(last_name) FROM 1 FOR 3) AS short_last,
    position('@' IN email) AS at_pos
FROM people
ORDER BY id;

username   | short_last | at_pos
--------------+------------+--------

 Alan.Turing  | Tur        |     12
 grace.hopper | hop        |     13
 linus        | TOR        |      6
 M.Hamilton   | Ham        |     11
 tim          | ber        |      4
(6 rows)

-------------------+------------+--------

Trim the last name before cutting, or ` Hamilton ` starts with a space. Then take 3 characters starting at position 1.
`position('@' IN email)` gives 0 for an email with no `@`.

steps.title: Building text
steps.body:
These functions build new text out of pieces:

- `replace(s, from, to)` swaps every `from` for `to`.
- `lpad(s, n, fill)` and `rpad(s, n, fill)` pad on the left or right until the text is `n` characters long.
- `concat_ws(sep, a, b, ...)` joins values with a separator between them.
- `repeat(s, n)` writes `s` out `n` times.

```sql
SELECT replace('555-0101', '-', '.'), lpad('7', 3, '0'),
    concat_ws(', ', 'Turing', 'Alan'), repeat('ab', 3);
-- 555.0101 | 007 | Turing, Alan | ababab
```

`lpad` takes text, so cast numbers first: `lpad(id::text, 5, '0')`. Watch out: when the text is already longer than `n`, both pads cut it down to `n` characters, so `rpad('Bartholomew', 8, '.')` is `Bartholo`.

`concat_ws` differs from `||` on NULL. `'a' || NULL` is NULL, but `concat_ws` skips NULL values, so `concat_ws(' ', 'Ada', NULL, 'King')` is `Ada King`.

example.title: Directory listing
example.prompt: Print each person's full name, the phone with dots, a five digit code made from the id, and the phone masked except its last four digits.
example.code:
SELECT initcap(concat_ws(' ', trim(first_name), trim(last_name))) AS full_name,
    replace(phone, '-', '.') AS dotted,
    lpad(id::text, 5, '0') AS code,
    repeat('*', 4) || right(phone, 4) AS masked
FROM people
ORDER BY id;
example.explanation: `concat_ws` puts one space between the trimmed names, then `initcap` fixes the case of the whole name. `replace` swaps the dash, `lpad` fills the id out to 5 characters with zeros, and `repeat('*', 4)` makes the mask that `||` joins to the last four digits.

practice.title: Name badges
practice.prompt:
Print a name badge line for each person in the people table.

1. Select the trimmed last name in capitals, then a comma and a space, then the trimmed first name with each word capitalized, as `badge` (for example `LOVELACE, Ada`).
2. Select the phone with every `-` replaced by a space as `spaced`.
3. Select the trimmed, capitalized first name padded on the right with dots to 8 characters as `padded`.
4. Sort by `id`.

Expected output:

```text
       badge        |  spaced  |  padded
--------------------+----------+----------
 LOVELACE, Ada      | 555 0101 | Ada.....
 TURING, Alan       | 555 0102 | Alan....
 HOPPER, Grace      | 555 0103 | Grace...
 TORVALDS, Linus    | 555 0104 | Linus...
 HAMILTON, Margaret | 555 0105 | Margaret
 BERNERS-LEE, Tim   | 555 0106 | Tim.....
(6 rows)
```
practice.starter:
-- TODO: select badge, spaced, and padded
SELECT first_name, last_name, phone
FROM people
ORDER BY id;
practice.solution:
SELECT concat_ws(', ', upper(trim(last_name)), initcap(trim(first_name))) AS badge,
    replace(phone, '-', ' ') AS spaced,
    rpad(initcap(trim(first_name)), 8, '.') AS padded
FROM people
ORDER BY id;

--------------------+----------+----------

 TURING, Alan       | 555 0102 | Alan....
 HOPPER, Grace      | 555 0103 | Grace...
 TORVALDS, Linus    | 555 0104 | Linus...

(6 rows)

badge         |  spaced  |  padded
----------------------+----------+----------

hints: Build the badge with `concat_ws(', ', ...)` and two arguments: the last name in capitals, then the capitalized first name.
`replace(phone, '-', ' ')` swaps each dash for a space.
Pad the same cleaned first name as in the badge. `rpad` adds dots to short names and cuts long ones to 8.

recap:
- `length`, `upper`, `lower`, `initcap`, and `trim` measure and clean text. Trim before you measure or cut.
- `left`, `right`, and `substring(s FROM start FOR count)` cut by position, counting from 1.
- `position(part IN s)` finds text and gives 0 when it is missing.
- `split_part(s, sep, n)` returns one field of text split on a separator.
- `replace`, `lpad`, `rpad`, `concat_ws`, and `repeat` build new text. Pads cut text that is too long.
- `concat_ws` skips NULL values, while `||` with NULL gives NULL.
